text:
alex: Heads-up: noticed requests to /v1/generate are getting double-counted for quota when clients send both `session_id` in header and as repeated query params. Example: /v1/generate?session_id=abc&session_id=abc. Our rewrite rules currently inject `x-client-session` from header and also preserve query params → backend sees two different keys and our quota middleware treats them as separate tokens.

maria: ugh, yeah we normalize headers but not query dedupe. Do we dedupe query params anywhere in the gateway? I think only path canonicalization is implemented.

tj: Not currently. We canonicalize path (lowercase + trim trailing slash) and sort query params, but we don't dedupe duplicate keys. Sorting alone still keeps duplicates.

alex: Minimal repro curl:```curl -v "https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate?session_id=abc&session_id=abc" -H "session_id: abc" -H "Authorization: Bearer x"``` Backend logs show `session_id` in headers and two query entries. Quota layer increments twice.

kai: That's bad. Could result in charge inflation for customers. Two quick paths: 1) dedupe query keys by first-occurrence (drop duplicates), or 2) prefer header over query and strip query key when header present. Which is safer for clients?

maria: leaning toward policy (2). Most SDKs send session_id as header. For public customers, stripping duplicate query keys if header present is backward-compatible and avoids changing URL semantics for other params. Also we should add an explicit audit log when we mutate request.

tj: Implementation note: route rewrite layer runs before auth/quota. If we strip query keys there, quota will see the corrected request. We'll need to update canonicalization middleware to both sort and dedupe. Pseudocode:```// sort + dedupe query params map<string, list<string>> params = parse(qs) for k, vs in params: if vs.length > 1: params[k] = [vs[0]] // keep first occurrence return build_qs(sorted(params))```

alex: +1 on keeping first occurrence. But we need config toggles per route: some endpoints rely on repeated params (rare but possible, e.g., ?tag=a&tag=b). So default behavior should dedupe only for specific keys (session_id, client_id, trace_id). We should expose `rewrite.query.dedupe_keys` per route in route config.

kai: Good call. Also add `rewrite.query.prefer_header_for_keys` list — keys which should be removed from query when header exists. That covers header preference.

maria: Can we also emit a telemetry flag for how often dedupe/strip triggered? We want to monitor breakage.

tj: Yep. Add a counter metric `gateway.rewrite.query_mutations{route,mutation_type}`. mutation_type in {dedupe,strip_header_prefer}. Also emit sample messages to `ops.rewrite-audit` index with original vs rewritten path limited to 1 per minute per route.

alex: I'll sketch a route config proposal for eng-runtime team:```routes: - path: /v1/generate  rewrite:    query:      sort: true      dedupe_keys: ["session_id","client_request_id"]      prefer_header_for_keys: ["session_id"]      audit_log: true```

maria: Love it. Quick question: what about caching/CDN keys? If we strip query params for session_id, we should ensure cache key doesn't include them in case edge caches vary.

tj: Cache key change is necessary. We'll add a `cache.key_include_query:false` override on routes that enable strip/prefer. We'll also add a migration doc so frontends using query session IDs know the behavior.

kai: Who's going to own rollout? Small canary behind the routing control plane makes sense. 1% traffic for 24h, check `gateway.rewrite.query_mutations` and customer-reported errors.

alex: I'll open a PR with the change set: gateway canonicalizer + config schema + metrics + docs. I'll add canary flags and a playbook for rollback. @maria @tj can you review?

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: `rewrite-dedupe-session` canary -> 1% at 2027-11-12T15:00Z (CI passed).

maria: Reviewing now, will comment on config schema.

tj: I'll review the canonicalizer changes. Also double-check edge cache behavior.

alex: Thanks. After PR merges we'll keep canary for 48h and then increase. If any spike in `api.quota.errors` or `rewrite-audit` unexpected entries -> rollback. :thumbsup:

kai: FYI added a follow-up note to the console UX backlog: show rewrite mutations in request inspector (so support can see when we stripped things).

maria: Nice, that will help debug customer tickets.

alex: Cool. I'll post PR link when ready.
